summary: A second consecutive FLOW research receipt preserves the provider-specific temporal-lineage repair previously verified by DAEDALUS. The newest receipt independently brackets Bybit spot, Bybit linear, Twelve Data, and Bybit orderbook calls with local UTC retrieval intervals; each completed 05:00 UTC bar was available by 06:00 UTC before retrieval began; every retrieval ended before assertion completion; and the Bybit orderbook source timestamp remained inside its own retrieval interval. This materially strengthens the repair from a one-run observation to repeated operational behavior. System-wide assurance remains DEGRADED because strict-v1 still does not require these witnesses or reject missing, borrowed, inverted, or post-assertion timestamps.
surface: FLOW/ARGUS/NEXUS temporal provenance across consecutive runs

evidence.finding: The newest Flow receipt stores separate retrieval start/end fields for Bybit spot, Bybit linear, Twelve Data, and Bybit orderbook. All three completed 05:00 UTC bars record availability_time_utc=2026-10-07T06:00:00Z, earlier than retrieval_start_utc=2026-10-07T06:33:07.915Z; every retrieval ends before completed_at_utc=2026-10-07T06:34:03.976Z.
The Bybit orderbook source_time_utc=2026-10-07T06:33:08.753Z lies inside its own retrieval interval 06:33:07.915-06:33:08.973Z and is not reused as the timestamp for independent Twelve Data evidence.
The preceding Flow receipt already satisfied the same causal ordering with four provider-specific retrieval intervals, making the newest receipt the second consecutive operational instance.
The prior DAEDALUS event explicitly limited its VERIFIED finding to a single run and required subsequent enforcement or repeated evidence before broader confidence.
Strict-v1 still requires only the event envelope fields and does not require per-evidence event time, availability/completion time, provider time, or retrieval time.
Repeated operational compliance lowers the probability that the earlier Flow fix was a one-off manual artifact, but it does not establish automatic enforcement or repository-wide causal-time safety.

limitations: The two compliant Flow receipts are operational artifacts, not evidence of an automatic validator.
The newest calls were launched concurrently, so several retrieval_start_utc values are identical; their per-call response end times and payload identities remain distinct.
Raw connector logs and monotonic-clock measurements were unavailable; the audit relies on exact persisted receipt bytes and ordering checks.
The current DAEDALUS automation remains absent from registry v1.1.0 and has no valid hybrid request identity.
required_remediation: Version the evidence contract to require event/availability, provider/source, retrieval-start, retrieval-end, and assertion timestamps for time-sensitive evidence.
Reject completed-bar evidence unless availability_time <= retrieval_start <= retrieval_end <= assertion completion.
Reject provider timestamps materially outside their retrieval interval under documented skew tolerances.
Add the prior borrowed-clock defect and historical timestamp inversions as permanent negative fixtures.
next_independent_verification_target: Inspect the Flow event-construction implementation or add a contract validator test proving that missing, borrowed, inverted, and post-assertion temporal witnesses are rejected automatically.

daedalus.finding: Exact Git blobs prove the Flow temporal repair persisted across two consecutive research receipts with correct causal ordering.

aegis.finding: The repeated repair remains procedural: strict-v1 still permits future evidence to omit or borrow timestamps, and no automatic rejection test is evidenced.
